articles.title: Broken Promises: RIP Instagram’s End-to-End Encrypted DMs
articles.summary: Microsoft patches 167 vulnerabilities including a SharePoint zero-day and Windows Defender's 'BlueHammer' flaw. When your Patch Tuesday requires scientific notation to count the CVEs, you know it's been a rough month for Redmond.

articles.title: Anti-DDoS Firm Heaped Attacks on Brazilian ISPs
articles.summary: Canvas education platform gets pwned nationwide, disrupting schools with ransom demands plastered on login pages. Nothing says 'back to school' like cybercriminals holding your homework hostage.

articles.title: Google disrupts hackers using AI to exploit an unknown weakness in a company's digital defense
articles.summary: Google catches hackers using AI to discover and weaponize zero-days for the first time. The machines aren't just coming for our jobs—they're coming for our exploits too.

articles.title: Victory! End-to-End Encrypted RCS Comes to Apple and Android Chats
articles.summary: Instagram kills its barely-used end-to-end encryption feature after years of promises. Meta's commitment to privacy apparently expires faster than a Snapchat message.

articles.title: Canada’s Bill C-22 Is a Repackaged Version of Last Year’s Surveillance Nightmare
articles.summary: EFF drops a hacker's guide to circumventing internet shutdowns. Because when governments cut the cables, the real engineers get creative with mesh networks and ham radios.

articles.title: LatAm Vibe Hackers Generate Custom Hacking Tools on the Fly
articles.summary: Canada repackages its surveillance nightmare as Bill C-22 after last year's privacy community beatdown. Same authoritarian flavor, now with 22% more 'lawful access' marketing spin.

articles.title: Patch Tuesday, April 2026 Edition
articles.summary: Scattered Spider member 'Tylerb' pleads guilty to wire fraud after SMS phishing spree. Another script kiddie learns that social engineering your way into telecom giants has consequences.

articles.title: Vietnam to develop domestic cloud so it can ditch risky overseas operators for government workloads
articles.summary: TeamPCP open-sources their Shai-Hulud worm on GitHub like digital Robin Hoods. Microsoft's code repository somehow missed malware being distributed on their own platform—peak irony achieved.

articles.title: Canvas breach spotlights cybercriminal appetite for student data
articles.summary: Official CheckMarx Jenkins plugin compromised with infostealer malware. When your security tool becomes the attack vector, someone's having a really bad day in DevSecOps.

articles.title: Official CheckMarx Jenkins package compromised with infostealer
articles.summary: NVIDIA confirms GeForce NOW breach with hackers selling customer data for $100K. Gaming in the cloud just got more expensive—and that's not counting the subscription fees.
